narrativeReportMd:
# Slot R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`Slot` keeps the same canonical resource identity and local element set, but it has one hard local instance-breaking change: `Slot.serviceType` is no longer a direct `CodeableConcept`; it is an R6 `CodeableReference(HealthcareService)`. Existing R4 instances that populate `serviceType` must be transformed before strict R6 validation.

## Scope
The assessment covers the base R4 and R6 `Slot` StructureDefinitions and local `Slot.*` elements. Inherited `Resource`, `DomainResource`, `Element`, and datatype infrastructure changes are excluded from findings and listed as out-of-scope.

## Main migration themes
The largest migration theme is representation change rather than removal: R4 `serviceType` codes become `serviceType.concept`, while R6 may also use `serviceType.reference` to point at `HealthcareService`. R6 also allows multiple `appointmentType` values, which is forward-compatible for R4→R6 instances but not losslessly representable when converting R6 data back to R4.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact finding is `Slot.serviceType` changing from `CodeableConcept` to `CodeableReference`, affecting validation, generated model types, serializers, FHIRPath/search extraction, and down-conversion. The second material finding is the `Slot.appointmentType` maximum cardinality increase from `1` to `*`, mainly a generated-code and R6→R4 round-trip risk.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important where an R6 `serviceType.reference` must be represented in R4. A migration can preserve R6 `serviceType.concept` values by unwrapping them, but a HealthcareService reference has no native R4 slot field unless mapped to a code, carried in an extension, or resolved through local business rules. Multiple R6 appointment types also require a policy when exporting to R4.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Both local breaking surfaces appear motivated by richer scheduling semantics. A less disruptive design could have preserved the R4 elements and added a new reference element or extension, but that would have fragmented the model rather than using R6's `CodeableReference` pattern and native repeating appointment types.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze `CodeableReference`, `HealthcareService`, and `Schedule` alongside Slot migration rules. Base `DomainResource` and `Resource` changes should remain owned by their own artifact reports.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `Slot` has a hard local breaking change in `serviceType`: populated R4 values must be wrapped as R6 `CodeableReference.concept`. The main migration concerns are `serviceType` representation/reference support, `appointmentType` becoming repeatable, and policy for down-converting richer R6 content. The largest uncertainty is official rationale and complete external terminology expansion, not the computable shape change itself.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should treat `Slot.serviceType` as a structural transform, not a simple type alias: R4 direct `CodeableConcept` values map to R6 `CodeableReference.concept`, while R6 `CodeableReference.reference` values require an extension, dereferencing strategy, or local mapping to a service code when exporting to R4. Generated clients also need to update `Slot.appointmentType` from a singleton optional property to a collection. Terminology validation pressure is not generally stronger in R6 for Slot-local bindings; `Slot.specialty` is weakened from preferred to example and `Slot.status` retains the same required code system membership.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for StructureDefinition-level element, cardinality, type, reference-target, and Slot.status code-set conclusions because they come directly from local core package JSON. Confidence is medium for detailed terminology and rationale because no official diff, full terminology server expansion, or narrative migration note was available. The R6 input is also a ballot build, so final R6 content may differ.

findings.title: Slot.serviceType changed from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference(HealthcareService)

semanticText.short: The type of appointments that can be booked into this slot ... overrides the value provided on the availability resource
semanticText.definition: The type of appointments that can be booked into this slot (ideally this would be an identifiable service - which is at a location, rather than the location itself). If provided then this overrides the value provided on the availability resource.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4 each `serviceType` array item is serialized directly as a `CodeableConcept`, for example with `coding` and/or `text` at the item level.

newState.summary: `Slot.serviceType` is a repeating `CodeableReference` that can carry either a concept or a `HealthcareService` reference.

semanticText.short: The type of appointments that can be booked into this slot ... overrides the value provided on the Schedule resource
semanticText.definition: The type of appointments that can be booked into this slot (ideally this would be an identifiable service - which is at a location, rather than the location itself). If provided then this overrides the value provided on the Schedule resource.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6 the same coded content must be nested under `serviceType.concept`, while a new `serviceType.reference` branch can point to a `HealthcareService`.

facts.note: The target profile is new because R4 had no reference branch on this element.

facts.newValue: serviceType[] item is a CodeableReference with concept and/or reference children

facts.note: Text appears to clarify that Slot serviceType overrides Schedule-level service type.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id and path are unchanged (`Slot.serviceType`), cardinality and binding are retained, and the only material local shape change is replacement of the type with `CodeableReference`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a hard R4→R6 validation break for any R4 `Slot` instance that actually contains `serviceType`: the R4 JSON shape has `coding`/`text` directly under each array item, while R6 permits `concept` and `reference` children on `CodeableReference`. Strict R6 parsers and validators will reject the old child names rather than treating the object as a valid CodeableReference. It is also a high R6→R4 risk because `serviceType.reference` to `HealthcareService` has no native R4 counterpart on `Slot`.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The risk is primarily scheduling/business interoperability: service-type loss or failed parsing can affect appointment discovery and booking workflows. Direct clinical safety risk was not identified from the base definition alone.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow Slot service type to be represented either by a code or by an identifiable HealthcareService resource while aligning with the R6 CodeableReference pattern.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `Slot.serviceType` as `CodeableConcept` and add a new optional base R6 `Reference(HealthcareService)` sibling for identifiable services.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: the Slot definition already says the service type is ideally an identifiable service, and R6 makes that representable through `CodeableReference(HealthcareService)`. The chosen design creates a hard representation break for populated R4 `serviceType` values. A less-breaking base design exists, but it has material long-term modeling and interoperability costs, so the break is probably justified rather than clearly unavoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base R6 design would keep the existing `Slot.serviceType` `CodeableConcept` shape and add a repeating optional sibling such as `serviceTypeReference` targeting `HealthcareService`, with guidance for reconciling code and reference values. That would let most R4 instances validate unchanged while supporting identifiable services. The tradeoff is that one fact would be represented in two same-resource fields, forcing consumers, search, validation, and profiles to decide how to handle overlap; the deprecated coded representation might never disappear and could accumulate with similar compatibility fields over time.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 payloads, but splits one scheduling concept across code and reference fields; duplicate representations need reconciliation and may persist indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R6 type is `CodeableReference` with targetProfile `HealthcareService` and cardinality `0..*`.
R6 CodeableReference defines `concept` as `CodeableConcept` and `reference` as `Reference`.

R6 defines a Slot `service-type-reference` SearchParameter over `Slot.serviceType.reference` targeting HealthcareService, supporting that the reference branch is intended for real resource references.

examples.examplesMd: The old-valid/new-invalid example focuses on the representation of `serviceType`; the other required Slot fields are included only to make the fragment realistic. Terminology membership was not validated with a live terminology server.

findings.narrativeMd: `Slot.serviceType` keeps the same name and repeating cardinality but changes datatype. This is disruptive because it is not just a generated class rename: the JSON/XML shape changes. R4 producers put a CodeableConcept directly in the array, while R6 producers put the CodeableConcept under `concept` or use `reference` to a HealthcareService. Implementers that deserialize Slot, index service type, or expose generated models must update both storage and transformation code.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with populated `serviceType` can be valid in R4 and invalid in R6 because `coding`, `text`, and other CodeableConcept children are no longer valid directly under `Slot.serviceType`. R6 concept-valued entries can be represented in R4 by unwrapping `concept`; R6 reference-valued entries are not natively representable in R4 and require an extension, dereferencing to a code, or loss of the reference identity. Strict parsers, JSON schema validators, FHIRPath expressions, search extraction, and generated enum/model bindings are all affected.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4→R6, transform every `Slot.serviceType[n]` CodeableConcept to `Slot.serviceType[n].concept`. Update FHIRPath and search indexing from `Slot.serviceType` to the appropriate R6 child path, normally `Slot.serviceType.concept` for token search and `Slot.serviceType.reference` for reference search. For R6→R4, unwrap `concept` values and define an explicit policy for `reference` values: preserve them in an extension, resolve the referenced HealthcareService to one or more service codes, or reject/down-scope the export as lossy. Test slots with absent serviceType, coded serviceType, reference serviceType, and mixed coded/reference repetitions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change was probably made to express the long-standing text that service type may ideally be an identifiable service. A backward-compatible alternative was available in principle: keep `serviceType` as CodeableConcept and add a new optional reference element or extension. That alternative avoids breaking existing payloads but leaves two fields to reconcile and weakens the unified CodeableReference modeling style used in R6.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review local policies for whether a HealthcareService reference should be preserved, dereferenced, or converted to a service-type code during R6→R4 exchange. This is likely implementation-specific and may require business-owner input.

findings.title: Slot.appointmentType is repeatable in R6

semanticText.short: The style of appointment or patient that may be booked in the slot (not service type)
semanticText.definition: The style of appointment or patient that may be booked in the slot (not service type).

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4 a Slot could advertise at most one appointment type. Generated models commonly expose this as a nullable/single CodeableConcept property.

semanticText.short: The style of appointment or patient that may be booked in the slot (not service type)
semanticText.definition: The style of appointment or patient that may be booked in the slot (not service type).
semanticText.comment: A slot may be allow multiple appointment types, but when booked, would only be used for one of the given appointment types.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6 a Slot can advertise multiple appointment types, while a booked appointment would use one of them.

facts.newValue: A slot may be allow multiple appointment types, but when booked, would only be used for one of the given appointment types.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element id, path, datatype, binding, and definition are stable; the material change is the maximum cardinality increase.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an R4→R6 validation break because every R4-valid singleton value is also valid under `0..*`. It is still a runtime/codegen change for R6 model adoption: generated properties and APIs move from a single optional CodeableConcept to a collection. It is a high R6→R4 representability risk whenever more than one appointment type is present because R4 has only one native slot field.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Appointment-type loss during down-conversion can affect scheduling and booking rules, for example a slot that supports both new and follow-up appointments may be simplified incorrectly.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent slots that can be booked for more than one appointment style while retaining one selected type when actually booked.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not an R4-to-R6 instance-breaking base-design issue; increasing `Slot.appointmentType` from `0..1` to `0..*` preserves every R4-valid singleton or absent value.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is reasonable because the new comment describes a real scheduling case: one slot may allow multiple appointment types even though a booked appointment uses one. The level of R4-to-R6 breakage is limited because the cardinality change is a widening, not a validation break for existing R4 instances. Remaining concerns are generated-model assumptions and lossy R6-to-R4 export, so the change is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed for R4-to-R6 instance compatibility because R4 `appointmentType` values are still valid under the wider R6 cardinality. A design that kept base `0..1` and used a standard extension or profile rule for additional appointment types would be a mitigation for R6-to-R4 conversion and singleton generated APIs, not a backward-compatible alternative to an R4-to-R6 base-design break. It would also make multi-type slot support less discoverable, less searchable, and less consistent across base implementations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping a singleton plus extension/profile would mainly reduce generated-code or R6-to-R4 churn, while making multi-type slots less visible and less interoperable.

evidence.detail: R6 adds explanatory text that a slot may allow multiple appointment types, but a booked appointment would use one of them.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example illustrates the shape that causes down-conversion ambiguity. The extension URL in the migration example is illustrative only, not a recommended canonical extension.

findings.narrativeMd: `Slot.appointmentType` changed from a singleton to a repeating element. This is a widening for R6 validation, so old R4 instances do not become invalid. The breaking effect is practical: generated model APIs, serializers, and business logic that assumed one appointment type must now handle a collection, and R6 content with multiple values cannot be exported to R4 without choosing, splitting, or extending.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-valid instances remain R6-valid with respect to this element because `0..1` is a subset of `0..*`. R6 instances with two or more `appointmentType` entries are not R4-valid. Runtime compatibility risk appears in codegen and business rules rather than base validation: clients must stop assuming a single value, and R4 export pipelines must detect multiplicity before producing a lossy singleton.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4→R6, wrap existing generated code accessors in collection-aware APIs or update application code to use the first/only element only when that is a documented local invariant. For R6→R4, decide whether to reject multi-valued slots, choose one value by priority, split the slot into multiple R4 slots, or preserve additional values in an extension. Test absent, singleton, and multi-valued cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 change is likely justified by the newly documented business case that a slot can support multiple appointment types. A backward-compatible extension-based design could have avoided changing the base cardinality, but would have made the multi-type behavior less visible and less interoperable across base implementations.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The local R6 comment has a minor wording issue (`may be allow`), but the intended semantic is clear. Review R4 export requirements before deciding whether multi-valued R6 slots need manual adjudication.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, type, kind, abstract flag, derivation, and baseDefinition remain `Slot` as a non-abstract `DomainResource` specialization. Governance status changed, but no rename/split/merge/removal was found.

The same local Slot element ids are present in R4 and R6: `identifier`, `serviceCategory`, `serviceType`, `specialty`, `appointmentType`, `schedule`, `status`, `start`, `end`, `overbooked`, and `comment`. No local element additions, removals, renames, or moves were identified.

No new local Slot-specific invariants were found. The visible changes to `dom-*`, `ele-1`, XPath fields, and inherited extension constraints are base `DomainResource`/`Element` concerns and are out of scope for Slot findings.

`Slot.schedule` remains a required `Reference(Schedule)`. The new `HealthcareService` reference capability is covered under the `Slot.serviceType` type-domain finding rather than as a separate schedule-reference change.

`Slot.status` remains required and the local SlotStatus CodeSystem has the same five codes in R4 and R6. `serviceCategory` and `serviceType` remain example bindings to the same value-set canonicals. `appointmentType` remains preferred to `http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/v2-0276`, but the R6 package did not include the corresponding THO ValueSet/CodeSystem file for code comparison. `specialty` binding weakening is noted separately as non-breaking.
No local Slot-defined element changed `isModifier`. Inherited modifier behavior is out of scope.
Local Slot-defined summary flags are unchanged. R6 explicitly supplies `mustSupport: false`, which does not impose a new support obligation.
No local Slot element gained or lost a fixed value, pattern, or default value.
No local Slot element gained maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue constraints.
No local Slot slicing or slice definitions were present in either base StructureDefinition.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Slot.specialty binding weakened from preferred to example
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Weakening a binding does not make existing R4 instances invalid in R6. It relaxes conformance expectations rather than narrowing the allowed coding domain.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Validators and quality checks may emit fewer interoperability warnings for specialty codes outside `c80-practice-codes`. The local compose code list in the ValueSet stayed the same, though four SNOMED display strings changed. Systems relying on preferred-code warnings should review their own profiles or validation policy.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Slot maturity/governance status advanced in R6
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The canonical identity and resource shape are not changed by the `status` and standards-status extension. R4 is draft/trial-use; R6 is active/normative in the inspected ballot package.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Normative status may affect governance, change-management expectations, and implementation confidence, but it is not itself an instance validation break.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Slot.status required ValueSet version changed but code set is stable
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The binding remains required, but the local R4 and R6 SlotStatus CodeSystems contain the same five codes: `busy`, `free`, `busy-unavailable`, `busy-tentative`, and `entered-in-error`.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Generated enums should still verify package-version-specific metadata and display/title changes, but no code removal or addition was found for the required status binding.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `Slot.serviceType` now depends on the R6 `CodeableReference` datatype. Datatype-level serialization and conversion behavior should be analyzed in the `CodeableReference` report.
R6 `Slot.serviceType.reference` targets `HealthcareService`. Down-conversion to R4 may require resolving or mapping HealthcareService type information.
The Slot service-type definition says Slot values override Schedule-level values. Schedule's own R4→R6 changes should be reviewed for consistent scheduling migration rules.
Inherited DomainResource/Resource constraint and inherited element flag changes were intentionally excluded from Slot findings and should be handled by base artifact reports.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4→R6 Slot diff, ballot disposition note, or committee rationale was available locally. Justification assessments are inferred from the computable definitions and supporting SearchParameters.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Use the official HL7 version-to-version diff or change notes for Slot and scheduling resources.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No live terminology expansion was performed. The local package includes enough data to confirm SlotStatus code stability and c80 compose-code stability, but some external terminology artifacts, including R6 `v2-0276` and THO service-type/service-category CodeSystems, were not present in the R6 core package.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run terminology expansion/comparison against the relevant R4 and R6/THO terminology packages.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is `6.0.0-ballot4`, not a final published R6 release. Ballot content may change before publication.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run the comparison against the final R6 package when available.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No local Slot example instances were found in the inspected core package search, and no production usage corpus was available. Prevalence estimates are therefore judgement-based.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Analyze implementation datasets or public test fixtures containing Slot instances.
